clinical_features.symptoms:
SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS 
*Non-specific 
*Consider PESI score to risk stratify 
*High index of suspicion especially in patients with 
-unexplained dyspnoea 
-tachypnoea 
-unexplained tachycardia 
-unilateral leg swelling 
 
INDICATIONS FOR THROMBOLYSIS 
Massive PE 
*Sustained hypotension (SBP < 90mmHg) 
for 15 minutes or requiring inotropic 
support 
*Persistent bradycardia with signs of shock 
*RV dysfunction on echo 
*Myocardial necrosis 
(Trop I > 0.4ng/ml or Trop T > 0.1ng/ml) 
Cardiac Arrest in PE 
ADJUNCT: 5mg nebulised nitrocine over 
15 mins, rpt PRN 
THROMBOLYTIC OF CHOICE 
ALTEPLASE (ACTILYSE®) 
Massive PE 
*≥65kg 
10mg bolus followed by 90mg infusion 
over 2 hours 
*<65kg 
Total dose of 1.5mg/kg 
10mg bolus and remainder of dose 
infused over 2 hours 
Cardiac Arrest: 50mg IVI as a stat dose 
Stable on low-dose pressor: consider 
10mg bolus, then 40mg over 2 hrs 
(0.5mg/kg) 
AGE ADJUSTED D-DIMER > 50 years 
AGE x 5 (divide by 1000 = mg/L stat lab 
units) 
Usual cutoff = 0.25 mg/L 
TRIMESTER ADJUSTED D-DIMER 
THRESHOLD 
1st - < 750 ng/ml (0.75mg/l)  
2nd - < 1000 ng/ml (1mg/l)  
3rd - < 1250 ng/ml (1.25mg/l)

PERC Score (Pulmonary Embolism Rule-Out Criteria) 
H – No Hormones (oestrogen) 
A – Age < 50 
D – No DVT/PE history 
C – No Coughing blood 
L – No unilateral Lower limb oedema 
O – Oxygen saturations ≥ 95% 
T – No Tachycardia ≥ 100bpm 
S – No Surgery / trauma within 28 days 
ALL need to be confirmed
